name: xero-bill-approved-to-subcontractor-email

trigger.authentication_note: Xero work.flowers. Only bound on the trigger — the workflow body never re-reads Xero, it just formats whatever the poll delivered.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger (New Bill), filtered to status=authorised, identical params to the classic Zap. A polling read trigger, so it has no webhook_url (expected — same as xero-draft-bill-to-slack-alert).

connections_note: dennis@work.flowers, GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@2.14.0 — same connection/version xero-invoice-paid-to-gmail-confirmation and xero-overdue-invoice-to-gmail-reminder use, and the same one the classic Zap's Gmail step was bound to. Do NOT confuse with the other Gmail connection in the account (`Gmail dennis@work.flowers`, GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@1.1.12), which gmail-attachments-to-drive-by-type uses on its trigger.
version_pinning_note: Newest versions of each direct dependency published at least 24h before build time, per the Vercel sandbox's pnpm minimumReleaseAge=1440 requirement.

tasks_per_run.every_other_authorised_bill: 0 (skipped in code before any app action — no line item coded to the Subcontractor Fees account)
tasks_per_run.note: No Xero re-read — the bill trigger already delivers the full invoice including LineItems, Contact and attachments.

filter.tightening: The classic filter used icontains (substring match), which would also match a hypothetical account code like "4900" or "1490". Tightened to an exact string match against a single Xero account code, since AccountCode values are short discrete codes, not free text — icontains bought nothing but false-positive risk here.

email.action: GoogleMailV2CLIAPI write `message` (Send Email) — sends, does not draft
email.from: Not set. The Gmail connection is dennis@work.flowers, so the default sender is already correct, and `from` is a dynamic enum that rejects an unvalidated literal (same reasoning as the sibling Xero Gmail Zaps).
email.to: Contact.EmailAddress (single recipient, matching the classic Zap — no cc/bcc).
email.attachments: bill.attachments[].file — the subcontractor's own uploaded invoice/receipt (Zapier 'file' hydrate references passed straight through to Gmail's `file` array input), NOT Xero's rendered InvoicePDF. Matches the classic Zap's `attachments[]file` mapping.

verified_cases.invoice: INV-26-0007 (Lantern Labs Pte. Ltd. / Peter Gao, me@petergao.com, SGD 60.43, one line item AccountCode 490, one attachment)
verified_cases.result: outcome 'dry-run'. Subject 'Invoice INV-26-0007 Approved'; body greets 'Hi Peter,' with Amount Due 'SGD 60.43' and Due Date '2026-08-29'; file carries the real attachment's hydrate reference string unmodified.
skipped, reason 'no invoice id in payload'. No Gmail call, no throw.

verified_cases.result: skipped, reason 'no line item coded to the Subcontractor Fees account (490)'. This is the filter working as intended — most approved bills (rent, software, etc.) should skip.

verified_cases.result: skipped, reason 'vendor has no email address in Xero'. No Gmail call, no throw.

send_path_note: The Gmail send step itself has NOT been fired for real — doing so would have emailed a real subcontractor a spurious approval confirmation. Composed-message verification above, plus the identical Gmail input shape (to/subject/body/body_type/file) exercised for real by the sibling Zaps xero-overdue-invoice-to-gmail-reminder (draft) and xero-invoice-paid-to-gmail-confirmation (send, same connection). Three bills are ALREADY authorised in the live org with a 490 line item (Ernest Choo INV009, Lantern Labs INV-26-0007, Nasri Nasir NIT-11) — none of these will retroactively get a confirmation, since a polling trigger primes its dedupe on first poll (deliberate, matches every other polling Zap in this repo — see xero-bank-transactions-to-zapier-table's zap.json). Watch the next bill actually approved after this publish.
dry_run_note: A manual run accepts `{"dryRun": true, "bill": {...}}` and returns the composed message without sending. The Xero trigger never sets `dryRun`, so production is unaffected.
description: Xero bill approved (AUTHORISED) with a Subcontractor Fees line item -> email the vendor a confirmation with invoice number, amount due, due date, and their own uploaded invoice attached. Migration of the classic 'Confirmation Email for Sub-contractor Invoices' Zap.

replaces_classic_zap.title: Confirmation Email for Sub-contractor Invoices
replaces_classic_zap.old_shape: XeroCLIAPI@2.21.0 bill (status: authorised) -> FilterAPI 'Subcontractor Fees' (LineItems[]AccountCode icontains "490") -> ZapierFormatterCLIAPI@1.0.8 date.formatting (DueDate -> YYYY-MM-DD) -> GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@2.14.0 write message. Four nodes.
replaces_classic_zap.status: The trigger node was NOT paused (still polling), but the filter, formatter and Gmail nodes were ALL paused: true in the export — so the classic Zap has never actually sent a confirmation. Turn the classic Zap off in the Zapier UI rather than unpausing it, or it and this workflow will both email the same subcontractor.
known_issues_fixed: Account-code filter tightened from icontains to an exact match (see filter.tightening above).
Date formatting moved from a paid Zapier Formatter step to free pure-code integer date arithmetic — same cost as the classic Zap intended, minus the formatter task.
No guard against an empty/test delivery of the trigger, or a vendor contact with no email address — now skips cleanly instead of sending a malformed or empty-recipient email.
Contact.FirstName is now the greeting's only source with a graceful '(there)' fallback rather than rendering 'Hi ,' if a contact has no FirstName set.
deliberately_preserved: Subject line, body wording, section layout and 'Thanks, Dennis' sign-off, verbatim.
Single recipient (Contact.EmailAddress only, no cc/bcc), plain-text body, signature delimiter on.
Attaching the subcontractor's own uploaded invoice/receipt file(s) rather than Xero's rendered PDF.

The 'Amount Due' label mapped to Xero's Total field (not AmountDue) — preserved from the classic Zap's exact field mapping; the two are equal immediately after a bill is authorised, before any payment is applied.

retired.reason: Its Xero POLLING trigger cost ~1,440 Xero API calls/day. Five such pollers on tenant 62699a8c exhausted Xero's 5,000-calls/day-per-tenant limit on 2026-08-06 (x-rate-limit-problem: day, x-daylimit-remaining: 0, x-minlimit-remaining: 60 — a daily quota exhaustion, not a burst), taking every Xero Zap in the workspace down for ~10 hours. A durable polling trigger cannot be throttled: the --trigger payload has no interval field, verified across all 43 live triggers in the account. This Zap's behaviour now runs as the `email-subcontractor` channel of the schedule-driven xero-invoice-alerts, which does the work of all three former pollers for ~24 calls/day.
retired.do_not_re_enable: Re-enabling would BOTH double-alert (xero-invoice-alerts already covers this) and put ~1,440 Xero calls/day back on the tenant. Change xero-invoice-alerts instead. Disabled, not deleted — the published version is intact and the trigger is `released`.
